To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the transcription factor EWg is alternatively spliced in Drosophilla and the different isoforms have differential activities in regulating gene expression; 2) the SC3 isoforms is the most active form in regulating gene expression and in rescuing viability and synaptic growth; and 3) a unique set of EWG target genes is identified whose expression is exclusively regulated by the SC3 form and is involved in regulating gene transcription.
the EWG transcription factor is involved in the regulation of a unique subset of genes, which is important for synaptic growth.
Alternative splicing in the brain is important for synaptic growth and that differential activity of EWG isoforms identifies a set of differentially regulated synaptic genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the function of the Drosophila erect wing (ewG) gene.
the identification of genes involved in the regulation of neuronal development.
the identification and characterization of genes that regulate synaptic growth and their function in the development of neuronal circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EWG transcription factor regulates a unique set of target genes involved in synaptic growth regulation.
the differential expression of EWG isoforms is associated with a unique gene set that is important for synaptic growth.
EWG regulates a subset of genes important for synaptic development that are not regulated by other EWG isoforms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
differential activity of EWG isoforms identifies a unique subset of genes that is differentially regulated and important for synaptic growth.
differential activity of EWG isoforms identifies a set of genes important for synaptic development and growth regulation.
the differential expression of EWG isoforms is important to regulate a specific set of genes involved in synaptic growth regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
differential expression of isoforms of the EWG transcription factor is associated with the expression of specific sets of genes.
alternative splicing can be a source for functional diversity in gene expression.
the activity of a transcription factor can be modulated by alternative splicing and that differential activity can lead to the identification of a unique set of target genes.
